paper_sections.title: Perceptual and categorical decision making: goal-relevant representation of two domains at different levels of abstraction.
Drift Diffusion Model and Domain Interaction
Parametric representation of stimulus features within the brain.
FPN dynamics as a function of feature salience.
FPN Representation of Multiple Sources of Information
Frontal-Parietal Dissociation and Cognitive Control Within FPN

description.value: The study examined how perceptual salience and categorical salience interact during perceptual categorization, and how frontoparietal BOLD activity represents decision-relevant information at different levels of abstraction.

design.value: Subjects performed a visual random-dot-motion categorization task in which motion coherence and motion direction relative to an oblique category boundary were independently varied. Behavioral responses were modeled with proportional-rate diffusion models, and BOLD activity was analyzed with voxelwise parametric, interaction, ANOVA, ROI, and deconvolution analyses.

description.value: The proportion of categorization responses that were correct.
The time taken to make the categorization response.
Assessment by a neurologist indicating normal neural anatomy.

source_definition.value: Perceptual salience was altered by changing dot-motion coherence: salience decreased as motion coherence decreased.

levels.value: 0%, 25%, 100%, and 1 intermediate coherence ranging from 12% to 15%; two subjects used two intermediate coherence values

source_definition.value: Categorical salience was manipulated by varying the direction of motion of the dots: salience decreased as the coherently moving dots moved closer to the boundary line.

levels.value: 0°, intermediate distance, 45°, 90° minus intermediate distance, and 90°

name.value: interaction between motion coherence and distance from category boundary

source_definition.value: The interaction variable in regression models of drift rate, and the interaction between perceptual and categorical information in the mixed-effects ANOVA.
Subjects were included as the random factor in the three-factor mixed-effects ANOVA.
Accuracies at different stimulus combinations, rank-ordered and averaged into four bins for parametric fMRI analysis.

association_direction.value: negative parametric effect, with BOLD activity increasing with decreasing accuracy

description.value: Ten subjects, ages 18-42 yr; 4 men and 8 women, participated in the study and gave written informed consent. All subjects had normal neural anatomy as assessed by a neurologist, were right-handed, and had normal or corrected-to-normal vision. One subject was excluded because of a high percentage of aborted trials; analyses were conducted on the remaining nine subjects.

inclusion_criteria.value: normal neural anatomy as assessed by a neurologist

exclusion_criteria.value: responded outside the response window in >20% of trials within each run in two scanner sessions

task_description.value: Subjects viewed a variable proportion of coherently moving dots on a background of randomly moving dots and categorized the direction of motion as either leftward or rightward of an oblique category boundary. Perceptual salience was manipulated through motion coherence and categorical salience through distance of motion direction from the category boundary.

design_type.value: Trials with jittered intertrial intervals; the boundary was presented in blocks

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to report their choice via a button press as quickly and accurately as possible, using the index or middle finger of their right hand. They were instructed to pay attention to the entire field of dots.

stimuli.value: A random dot kinematogram with dots moving in one of 16 directions, with variable proportions of coherently moving dots on a background of randomly moving dots. The category boundary was an oblique line inclined at either 45° or 135° from the horizontal.

instrument.value: Siemens MAGNETOM Trio 3-T MR scanner at the Henry H. Wheeler, Jr. Brain Imaging Center, using a 12-channel phased-array coil

description.value: Functional images consisted of 32 slices acquired with a single-shot gradient echoplanar imaging protocol in a contiguous order. A projector was used to display the image on a translucent screen placed within the scanner bore behind the head coil, and responses were recorded with an MRI-safe fiber-optic response pad.

mr_acquisition_type.value: 32 slices acquired in a contiguous order

instrument.value: Siemens MAGNETOM Trio 3-T MR scanner with a 12-channel phased-array coil

description.value: Anatomical images consisted of 160 slices acquired with a T1-weighted MP-RAGE protocol.

fMRI preprocessing was performed with both AFNI and FSL. Functional images were converted to four-dimensional NIfTI format, slice-time corrected, motion corrected, smoothed, coregistered to the structural image, and normalized to the MNI_N27 standard volume.

steps.value: Functional images were converted to four-dimensional NIfTI format.
Images were corrected for slice timing offsets.
Motion correction was carried out with AFNI 3dvolreg, using the mean image of the first run in the series as the reference volume.
Images were smoothed with a 5-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.
Coregistration was performed with AFNI 3dAllineate using the local Pearson correlation cost function for fMRI-to-MRI structural alignment.
The subsequent inverse transformation was used to warp the anatomical image to functional image space.
Anatomical images were normalized with FSL fnirt to the MNI_N27 standard volume.
The same normalization parameters were applied to native-space statistical maps for group statistical maps.

model_settings.value: A′, k, and TR were assumed constant across all stimulus conditions, while x represented the interaction of perceptual and categorical information. Twenty values of x represented the 20 stimulus combinations derived from 4 coherence values and 5 distances from category boundary; one value each of A′, k, and TR was fit.

estimator.value: An iterative procedure designed to optimize the log-likelihood of the diffusion model fit

model_settings.value: Values for x representing distance from category boundary were obtained by fitting behavior at the highest motion coherence and used at all other motion coherence values. A′, k, and TR were fit anew for each motion coherence in a two-step process.

estimator.value: An iterative procedure designed to optimize the log-likelihood of the diffusion model fit

model_settings.value: Values for x representing motion coherence were obtained by fitting behavior at the highest distance from category boundary and used at all other distances. A′, k, and TR were fit anew for each distance from category boundary in a two-step process.

estimator.value: An iterative procedure designed to optimize the log-likelihood of the diffusion model fit

hrf_model.value: gamma probability density function peaking at 6 s

model_settings.value: The four coherence values and five unique distance values were modeled with separate regressors. Tests of linear trends used vectors transformed to zero mean with a sum of squares equal to 1. Only correct trials were evaluated for univariate analyses, except for the accuracy map.

Subject-level statistical maps were mapped to the MNI template and subjected to group-level analyses. Mapwise significance was P < 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons using a 20-voxel cluster-size correction after an initial threshold of P < 0.001 uncorrected.

Motion coherence and distance from boundary comprised the fixed factors and subjects the random factor. The ANOVA was also repeated after excluding zero-motion-coherence and zero-category-distance conditions.

Hemodynamic responses beginning at stimulus onset were estimated for each combination of motion coherence and distance from category boundary using piecewise B-spline basis functions separated by 100-ms intervals for 20 s after onset.

title.value: Parameter ranges across subjects for each model version

footer.value: Values are medians (interquartile ranges) for each model parameter (x, stimulus strength; k, sensitivity; A′, decision threshold; TR, nondecision time) for the 3 model versions, where lo and hi refer to lowest and highest stimulus salience levels. For the Interaction model, x (lo) and x (hi) refer to the lowest and highest levels of combined perceptual and categorical salience, respectively. For this model, a single value of k, A′, and TR was subsequently fit across all combinations of perceptual and categorical salience. For the Distance model, x (lo) and x (hi) refer to the lowest and highest levels of categorical salience, respectively. For the other parameters in this model, lo indicates the lowest and hi indicates the highest level of perceptual salience. Conversely, for the Coherence model x (lo) and x (hi) refer to the lowest and highest levels of perceptual salience, respectively. For the other parameters in this model, lo indicates the lowest and hi indicates the highest level of categorical salience.

description.value: Reports parameter ranges across subjects for the Interaction, Distance, and Coherence diffusion-model versions.

footer.value: Values are median regression coefficients obtained by regressing model drift rates against motion coherence (perceptual), distance from category boundary (categorical), and their interaction with all 20 stimulus combinations included and with lowest-salience conditions in both domains excluded, with numbers of subjects (of 9) exhibiting significant regression coefficients in parentheses.

description.value: Reports regression coefficients for perceptual, categorical, and interaction effects in the diffusion-model variants.
